content.title: Orlando Magic Dominate Charlotte Hornets in Play-In, Will Take On Detroit Pistons in First Round of Playoffs | Orlando Magic
content.text: DETROIT – As the buzzer sounded at Little Caesar’s Arena, signaling the Orlando Magic’s Game 1 victory, fans of the franchise scattered throughout the building and across social media celebrated the team’s stellar wire-to-wire victory.In Orlando’s locker room, the mood was much more dialed back.Paolo Banchero delivered a short but simple message to his teammates: “Don’t start drinking the Kool-Aid.” By that, the superstar forward meant that while taking Game 1 was nice, there’s still a lot of work to be done.The eight-seed Magic (1-0) will attempt to secure another victory in the Motor City before the series shifts to the City Beautiful when they square off with the one-seed Detroit Pistons (0-1) on Wednesday at 7 p.m. ET. The contest will air on ESPN.“We can’t overreact to one win in Game 1,” said Banchero. “It’s a long series. We all know how the media is. They’ll jump back onboard. So, just reminding guys, don’t buy into that. Stay locked in on the mission and don’t react to one game. We have to come out and do it again (tonight).”In addition to bringing the same energy and effort it displayed in Game 1 into Game 2, Orlando will also look to duplicate its presence in the paint. Both teams attempted 36 shots in that area on Sunday, but the Magic outscored the Pistons 54-34 in the paint, while shooting 67 percent from that region.Ball security will also once again be paramount against a Detroit team that likes to generate easy offense in transition. In the series opener, Orlando committed just 12 turnovers. However, to show the potency of the Pistons in that regard, Detroit scored 18 points off of those giveaways.“In the half court, (we have to continue) to pack the paint,” said Magic forward Franz Wagner. “It’s pretty simple. Having pressure on the ball makes it harder (for them) to get in there (for their) ballhandlers. Something we can do better is take care of the ball. That’s how they generate a lot of points in the paint throughout the season.”Orlando will need to slow down Cade Cunningham, who is the engine that makes the Pistons' offense go. The two-time All-Star fired off 39 points in the opener, but was limited to just four assists. This season, he was one of only two players in the NBA to average at least 23 points, nine assists and five rebounds per game. The other was three-time MVP Nikola Jokic. Cunningham’s 9.9 assists per outing ranked second in the league, only behind Jokic.The Magic will also need to be dialed into the offensive game plan to penetrate a Pistons unit that boasted the Eastern Conference’s best defensive rating (108.9). They led the NBA this season in blocks (6.4) and steals (10.4) and were second in deflections (20.5).“I think you have to understand how desperate Detroit is going to come out and be,” said Magic guard Desmond Bane. “How physical they’re going to be. They want to protect their home court, of course. It’s our job to come in here and get the job done tonight.”IN AND OUT: Jonathan Isaac (left knee; sprain) is doubtful for Orlando.Detroit has a clean injury report heading into Game 2.QUOTES TO NOTE: “It’s one game. In a seven-game series you have to win four. It’s a good start, but you still have to win four games. So, we know it’s important that we come (in tonight) and win the second game.” – Magic guard Anthony Black“It’s one game at a time. It’s the reality that, yeah, you did the Game 1 win, but now you have to go and figure out how to get a Game 2. There’s obviously going to be the positive talk about what you’ve done and thinking there’s reasons to celebrate. But at the end of the day, it’s one game. And that’s the most important piece that we’ve talked about. Just taking it one game at a time.” – Magic head coach Jamahl MosleyKEY STATS: Orlando’s Game 1 victory was its first road playoff win since April 13, 2019 in Toronto.The Magic never trailed in their win over the Pistons. It was the first time in the play-by-play era (since 1997-98) that a one seed did not lead at any point in their playoff opener (per ESPN Insights).HOW TO WATCH: Watch the contest on ESPN.
